content:
The Circles chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Circles tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Circles

Chords and tangents, circle theorems (angle at centre, semicircle), cyclic quadrilaterals, and arc/sector measures.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Angle at the centre = twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc.
  • Angle in a semicircle = 90°.
  • Tangent ⟂ radius at the point of contact; two tangents from a point are equal.
  • Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles sum to 180°.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Forgetting the tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
  • Using the inscribed angle where the central angle is needed (or vice versa).
  • Missing the cyclic-quadrilateral property.

faq.q: What is the angle in a semicircle?
faq.a: A right angle (90°) — the diameter subtends 90° at any point on the circle.

faq.q: What is special about a tangent?
faq.a: It touches the circle at exactly one point and is perpendicular to the radius drawn to that point.
